#### 1. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.473)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6794361)

**Proposed mechanism:** SHANK3 (HGNC:10716) —DISRUPTS→ postsynaptic density organization (GO:0051960); STXBP1 (HGNC:11332) —DISRUPTS→ regulation of synaptic vesicle transport (GO:0099504); postsynaptic density organization (GO:0051960) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); regulation of synaptic vesicle transport (GO:0099504) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); postsynaptic density organization (GO:0051960) —BINDS→ regulation of synaptic vesicle transport (GO:0099504). Loss-of-function mutations in SHANK3 disrupt postsynaptic density organization, contributing to intellectual disability. Simultaneously, loss-of-function mutations in STXBP1 disrupt the regulation of synaptic vesicle transport, leading to seizures. Both postsynaptic density organization and synaptic vesicle transport are critical, interconnected processes for neuronal function, and their disruption converges to cause overlapping phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in SHANK3 are exclusively associated with Phelan-McDermid syndrome and mutations in STXBP1 are exclusively associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 4, and no other shared molecular pathway or process is identified that links these two distinct genetic origins to the shared phenotypes, then this mechanistic hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs121918242 (SHANK3 NM_032003.3:c.2299G>A, p.(Gly767Arg)) has a GMAF of 0.0001 in European populations. If a pathogenic variant with a significantly higher frequency (e.g., >1%) were identified in gnomAD and linked to either disease, it would challenge the rare disease hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular pathways disrupted by SHANK3 and STXBP1 mutations could lead to the development of targeted therapies that address common downstream deficits, potentially benefiting patients with both Phelan-McDermid syndrome and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 4.
